description: Immutable ordered opaque sRGB8 palette sampled by a phase in cycles, with linear encoded-channel interpolation and fixed RGB24 quantization.

colors.evidence: mountain4#2, pelines#1 and Cuadricula#1 use ordered colour lists. Preserve caller artwork and duplicate entries. RGB24 and opaque-only scope are portable design choices, not a claim about every host colour type. Nonempty length <=2^31-1 is a cross-target index representability bound, not an artistic range or allocation guarantee.

phase.evidence: Source helpers use entry coordinates; public cycles remove palette-length coupling. mountain4 dc random(0.099,0.1) -> random(0.3,0.4) reports moderate colour change with fixed geometry, but does not establish a recommended phase/rate range. pelines palette replacement changes background too; Cuadricula experiments are unscored.

behavior.construction: Validate passive object with exactly colors; colors must be an array of 1..2147483647 mathematical integral values in 0..16777215. Integral floating values accepted; booleans rejected. Validate keys, array shape/length, then entries in order. Snapshot and retain supplied order including duplicates. Normalize zero to +0. No default palette. Serialize only {colors:[...]}, returning detached data each time.
behavior.query_validation: Query is one finite binary64 phase scalar. Reject bool, null, string, array, object and nonfinite values with INVALID_QUERY. Convert permitted native number to binary64 before validation; an overflowing Python integer is INVALID_QUERY. Validate even for a single-entry palette. Unsupported native call arity is a host-language call error, not an interchange-data result.
behavior.wrapping: Let n be palette length. Compute f=phase-floor(phase) as one separately rounded binary64 subtraction. Normalize f==0 to +0. If f==1 from rounding a tiny negative phase, set f=0. Compute x=f*n as one separately rounded binary64 multiplication; if x==n set x=0. Let i=floor(x), t=x-i (separately rounded), j=0 if i+1==n else i+1. Never cast the unwrapped phase to an integer index. All finite phases are valid; large phases may lose all fractional precision and sample the first entry. No epsilon or reflection/absolute value. Integer-shift periodicity is guaranteed only when the shifted binary64 phase preserves the fractional part.
behavior.color: Entries and result are unsigned RGB24 integers 0xRRGGBB, with each encoded sRGB8 channel in 0..255. Interpolate encoded channels directly; no gamma decode, HSB conversion, alpha, premultiplication or host colorMode. For each R,G,B channel a,b: d=b-a; p=t*d; v=a+p; q=floor(v+0.5), every arithmetic step separately rounded binary64. Pack qR*65536+qG*256+qB as an exact integer. No FMA/reassociation; IEEE round-to-nearest ties-to-even for primitive operations, explicit final half-up channel quantization. Result integer compares exactly, including canonical positive zero. With one entry return its value after validating the phase.
behavior.ownership: No mutable input/output alias or externally observable cache. Reordered/repeated queries and interleaved palettes produce the same values. Native scalar query returns a colour value and requires no query-container allocation. Caller mutation of serialized colors does not affect the palette.
behavior.environment: No RNG, noise, time, rendering, assets, global colour state or implicit seed. Opacity is caller mark style. Renderer adapters must explicitly convert RGB24 to their native colour representation; this contract does not validate any adapter.
behavior.cost: O(n) validation and snapshot storage at construction and serialization; O(1) bounded work per query. No eager sampled ramp. Length representability does not promise an allocation succeeds on a particular machine; ordinary resource exhaustion is not an INVALID_INPUT semantic error.
behavior.native_representations: Passive interchange data only, not callbacks/accessors/proxies. Java accepts boxed Byte/Short/Integer/Long/Float/Double and native double query; unsupported Number subclasses rejected before lossy coercion. Python accepts int/float but not bool; entries validated as mathematical integers before narrowing. JavaScript requires number. Native palette containers are Java List, JavaScript Array, and Python list/tuple; serialization is object/map with a newly owned list/array. No packed signed ARGB input or string hex parsing. Query schemas describe canonical binary64 interchange values after permitted native numeric normalization; raw JSON token parsing is outside this operation. A Python integer just above maximum binary64 may round to that finite maximum and is accepted, while an integer that overflows conversion is INVALID_QUERY. The schema is not a raw arbitrary-precision-token parser.
behavior.compatibility: Cycles, negative wrap and quantization are deliberate portable semantics. Source v/n conversion can alter floating arithmetic; no Processing lerpColor or source-pixel identity claim. Selected membership establishes the computation, not those exact native numerics.
behavior.native_api: Java org.procedurals.color.CyclicPalette.create(params), JavaScript cyclicPalette(params), Python cyclic_palette(params), each returning immutable sampler with sample(phase) and serialize(). Java may overload sample(Object) and sample(double) for dynamic validation and scalar hot path. Native error classes expose code; no alternate coordinate mode or alias factory.

errors.INVALID_INPUT: Invalid object keys, colors container/length, or any nonintegral, boolean, nonfinite or out-of-range RGB24 entry. No partial palette returned.
errors.INVALID_QUERY: Phase is not a permitted finite binary64 scalar. No partial output.

reproduction.acceptance: CP1 recolouring of retained geometry and alternate-mark transfer; source mountain4/pelines/Cuadricula motivate technique only. The JAVA2D CP1 example is validated separately in cp1_example; other hosts and source baseline suites remain unvalidated.

cp1_example.scope: Actual JAVA2D example/edit/transfer only; motivating corpus baseline suites and other hosts are not certified.

review.status: Sol approved actual contract and independently matched all 115 scalar outputs and 24 index vectors in JavaScript; Fraction fixture regeneration byte-stable. Root accepted.
